A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TCD-DL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Retained content can be matched reliably despite rewriting, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and analyses of K562 gene-expression data.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds intervention analyses and small-graph experiments, including evaluation on Sachs.

M1.justification: The axial Transformer, dot-product cause scores, binary-cross-entropy learning, and subsampling/ensembling algorithms remain unchanged. v2 adds labeling and loss-masking details, but does not establish a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds the Sachs dataset with 11 variables and a simultaneous three-node intervention scenario used during training and testing. These extend the retained coverage of simulated networks, E. coli, yeast, and K562; the analytic mechanism families were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds evaluated comparisons with PC, GIES, and TCD-DL (direct), concentrated in the new small-graph experiments. The existing large-scale GRN comparator set remains unchanged. Figure 2 also revises its comparator description from Wu et al.'s method to a matched Transformer counterpart.

E3.justification: New small-graph protocols include 10-node synthetic training, 100-observation Sachs evaluation, and pairwise binary accuracy, with PC using observational samples only. Section 5.4 adds fixed-size intervention sweeps with simulator dropout disabled, three-node interventions during training and testing, and causal-direction evaluation. Existing main GRN settings are retained.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix C.1's limited intervention-replacement study is replaced by broader analyses of intervention sample counts, intervened-node ratios, target/ancestor intervention categories, simultaneous interventions, and causal-direction accuracy. The training-source ablations, distance analysis, and hyperparameter sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random seeds for expression-data sampling and standard deviations in the main benchmark table. The hyperparameter error bars are retained in v1 Figure 8/v2 Figure 9. No changed repeated-run counts or statistical estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes high-fidelity validation AUROC from 89.6 to 92.6, while v1 Table 9/v2 Table 10 retain the main benchmark scores. Added findings include 76.4% Sachs accuracy and 93.7% AUROC under three-node interventions. The original Appendix C.1 result entries disappear; the replacement intervention results use different conditions and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the intervention-based definition of causes with graph ancestors, separately defines marginal causes, and adds a proposition and proof relating the two. v2 explicitly assumes no latent variables or selection bias. The local-inference proposition now requires retaining all root variables and specifies a marginalization rule; the complexity bound is retained.

C1.justification: The central learning, scalability, and GRN-generalization contributions remain. The abstract and introduction reframe the output as potential regulators without full graph reconstruction, while replacing assumption-elimination language with an acknowledgment that the model learns assumptions embedded in simulated data.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges incomplete human-GRN ground truth and that STRING associations do not establish causal direction. It adds discussion of identifiability with limited interventions and interpretations of the new partial- and multiple-intervention findings. These substantially qualify the applicability and evidential meaning of the predictions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents topological sorting for labels, target-position loss exclusion, zero-threshold decisions, and architecture/parameter/data matching for Figure 2. It also supplies Sachs data-source information. The core hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and repository-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially expands local causal discovery and GRN positioning. It explicitly distinguishes the proposed unordered ancestral set from Magliacane et al.'s ancestral ordering, discusses scalable PC and additional local methods, and adds a dedicated GRN-inference discussion. These changes refine the relationship to prior research beyond citation additions alone.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into setup, unseen-structure generalization, extended OOD analysis, and additional analysis. Appendix material is regrouped, and the title adds Large-Scale.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel intervention Figure 8, architecture Figure 10, and small-graph Table 9. It revises the method schematic, MYC diagram, legends, captions, and some table placement. The overall page format and most existing plots and appendix network visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the paper by separating ancestral candidates from intervention-changing causes, stating assumptions, and acknowledging STRING's validation limits. The expanded intervention analyses and conventional-baseline comparisons address important weaknesses in practical validation. A material gap remains: Proposition 2 requires retaining all roots, while Algorithm 2 does not enforce that condition. Nevertheless, the clearer scientific target and stronger examination of practical limitations provide substantial overall gains.
